headline: Harvard study: Largest U.S. data centers emit more carbon than all of Denmark
outlet: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
where: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
claim: US hyperscale data centers emitted about 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 in one year, mostly from fossil-fuel power, comparable to Denmark's annual emissions.
notes: published 2026-11-16 (university news release, page date read via WebFetch). Peer-reviewed study in Nature Sustainability (lead author Guidi, corresponding author Dominici). Estimate, not a direct measurement: attributed from plant-level generation data for 2024-2025 at 403 facilities; the study uses 2023 EPA data and says figures are likely understated for today. Coverage ties the buildout to AI demand; the study covers hyperscale data centers generally, not AI-only facilities. The university is the study's own institution, so the release is an interested party's own work.

claim: US hyperscale data centers emitted about 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 in one year, mostly from fossil-fuel power, comparable to Denmark's annual emissions.
